issues.description: Name mismatch for the global compute-table variable in the decision-diagram module. The template dd_simulation.py imports CT from .dd (line 51), and the rest of the simulator code expects a symbol named CT. However, the template dd.py defines the compute table as _CT (underscore prefix) instead of CT, so CT is not available for import. This will cause an import error / NameError and blocks students from running or implementing the simulator. The solution repository uses CT (no underscore), showing the intended name.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the compute-table variable name consistent. Change the declaration in template_repository/dd.py from `_CT = ComputeTable()` to `CT = ComputeTable()` (or update all imports and references to use `_CT` instead). Using `CT` (no underscore) matches dd_simulation.py and the solution and avoids import/name errors.

issues.description: The compute-table global is named inconsistently between the template dd.py and the code that imports it. In template_repository/dd.py the ComputeTable instance is created as `_CT = ComputeTable()` (underscore-prefixed), but template_repository/dd_simulation.py imports `CT` (no underscore). The reference implementation (solution_repository/dd.py) uses `CT = ComputeTable()` (no underscore). This mismatch will cause an immediate import/name error for students working from the template and creates unnecessary confusion about the intended global compute-table identifier (is it `_CT` or `CT`?).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the compute-table global name consistent across artifacts. Change `_CT = ComputeTable()` in template_repository/dd.py to `CT = ComputeTable()` (preferred, to match the solution), or alternatively update imports in dd_simulation.py to import `_CT`. Using `CT` (no underscore) everywhere aligns template and solution and avoids student-facing import/name errors.
